subject: chemistry
title: Metals and non-metals
key_idea: Elements that react to form positive ions are metals. Elements that do not form positive ions are non-metals. Metals are to the left and towards the bottom of the periodic table. Non-metals are towards the right and top.

blocks.text: The periodic table divides the elements into metals and non-metals. The division follows from the atomic structure of the elements.

items.meaning: An element that reacts to form positive ions.
An element that does not form positive ions.

items: The majority of elements are metals.
Metals are found to the left and towards the bottom of the periodic table.
Non-metals are found towards the right and top of the periodic table.
Group 1 and Group 2 elements, and the transition elements, are metals. Groups 4 to 0 are towards the right, so they are mostly non-metals. Tin and lead are metals lower down Group 4.
Metal atoms typically have few electrons in the outer shell. They lose these electrons to form **positive ions**.
Non-metal atoms typically have more electrons in the outer shell. They gain electrons to form **negative ions**, or share electrons.
Sodium (2,8,1) loses one electron to become Na⁺. Chlorine (2,8,7) gains one electron to become Cl⁻.
Metals form positive ions. Non-metals do not.
Metals are to the left and towards the bottom. Non-metals are towards the right and top.
Metal atoms lose outer electrons. Non-metal atoms gain or share them.

blocks.text: Metals and non-metals differ in their physical properties and in their chemical properties.

rows: Malleable (can be bent and shaped) and ductile

items: Not every metal fits every property. Gallium is a metal that melts below 100 °C.
A metal reacting with a non-metal forms an ionic compound, such as magnesium chloride.

diagram.alt: Sort each statement into metals or non-metals.

Found towards the right and top of the table
Gains electrons to form negative ions

items: Metals conduct, are malleable and ductile, and are usually strong with high melting points.
Non-metals are poor conductors and brittle when solid.
Metals form positive ions. Non-metals form negative ions or no ions.

blocks.text: A metal is more reactive if its atoms lose their outer electrons more easily. Position in the table links to this.

blocks.label: A metal and a non-metal react
where: Each sodium atom loses one electron to form Na⁺.
Each oxygen atom gains two electrons to form O²⁻.
Two sodium atoms are needed for each oxygen atom.

blocks.text: Why metals lower down a group are more reactive

items.text: Atoms lower down a group have more shells of electrons.
The outer electron is further from the nucleus and there is more shielding.
The attraction between the nucleus and the outer electron is weaker.
The outer electron is lost more easily, so a positive ion forms more easily.

items: Metals react by losing outer electrons to form positive ions.
Further down a group, the outer electron is further from the nucleus and is lost more easily.

checks.q: Describe where the non-metallic elements are found in the periodic table.
checks.a: Towards the right and the top of the periodic table.

checks.q: Give two physical properties of metals.
checks.a: Any two from: conducts electricity, conducts heat, malleable, ductile, shiny, strong, high melting point.

checks.q: Describe what happens to sodium atoms and to chlorine atoms when sodium reacts with chlorine.
checks.a: Each sodium atom loses one electron to form Na⁺. Each chlorine atom gains one electron to form Cl⁻. Both ions have full outer shells.

exam_phrases: towards the right and the top (non-metals)
to form Na⁺ and O²⁻ / ions with full outer shells
outer electrons are further from the nucleus, so less strongly attracted
positive ions are formed more easily

mistakes.wrong: A physical property of metals is that they form positive ions.
mistakes.right: Forming positive ions is a chemical property, and chemical properties are ignored when physical ones are asked for. Give conducts electricity, malleable, ductile, shiny, strong or a high melting point.

mistakes.wrong: Calcium reacts more vigorously than magnesium because calcium atoms are larger.
mistakes.right: 'Atoms are larger' is ignored. Say the outer electrons are further from the nucleus, so less strongly attracted, so positive ions form more easily.

mistakes.wrong: Gallium is a metal, so its melting point is high.
mistakes.right: Gallium has a melting point below 100 °C, which is not typical of most metals.

worked_example.question:
Explain what happens to sodium atoms and to oxygen atoms when sodium reacts with oxygen to produce sodium oxide (Na₂O).

Answer in terms of electrons.
answer_points: A sodium atom loses one electron.
An oxygen atom gains two electrons.
So two sodium atoms react with each oxygen atom.
Na⁺ and O²⁻ ions form (sodium ions and oxide ions), with full outer shells.
worked_example.tip: One mark each. Say what each atom does with its electrons, then give the ratio and the ions formed.

exam_phrases: it is on the left (of the periodic table)

mistakes.wrong: Calcium is a metal because it is in period 4.
mistakes.right: The period does not show it. Say calcium is on the left of the table, in group 2 (column 2).

mistakes.wrong: Non-metals are on the left of the periodic table.
mistakes.right: Metals are on the left. Non-metals are towards the right.

worked_example.question: State how you know that calcium is a metal from its position in the periodic table.
answer_points: It is on the left, in Group 2 (column 2).
worked_example.tip: Use the position: left of the table, or Group 2.

exam_phrases: low density and good electrical conductor
one electron in the outer shell (metal atom)
has more protons than electrons (positive ion)
lithium fluoride contains metal and non-metal elements

mistakes.wrong: Aluminium is best for pylon cables because it is light and a good conductor.
mistakes.right: The mark needs both properties: low density and good electrical conductor. 'Light' is not allowed for low density, and 'good conductor' alone is ignored.

mistakes.wrong: Particle D is an ion because it has a different mass number.
mistakes.right: An ion has a different number of protons and electrons. Particle D has more protons than electrons.

worked_example.question:
Look at the information about some particles.

Particle A: atomic number 11, mass number 23, 11 electrons, electronic structure 2.8.1.
Particle D: atomic number 13, mass number 27, 10 electrons, electronic structure 2.8.

Particle A is a metal atom, particle D is an ion.

Explain why.
answer_points: Particle A has one electron in its outer shell (energy level), so it is a metal.
Particle D has more protons than electrons, so it is an ion.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each particle. Use the numbers of outer electrons, protons and electrons.
